kaps_punt: Skakel tussen die holistiese en Westerse vorme van die genesing van vandag

items.bewering: Twee maniere van genees staan vandag naas mekaar in ons land.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: Pinkoane, Greeff & Koen 2012, African Journal of Traditional, Complementary and Alternative Medicines (via repository.nwu.ac.za/handle/10394/41445): 80-90% of black patients use both traditional healers and biomedical personnel; Traditional Health Practitioners Act 22 of 2007 (source.acts.co.za) regulates traditional practice alongside the biomedical system.

items.bewering: Inheemse genesing kyk na die hele mens en behandel sy gees en liggaam saam. Dit kyk ook na sy gevoelens en na die mense om hom.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Traditional healers of Southern Africa' and Google Arts & Culture 'Who are Sangomas and Inyangas?': the inyanga is a herbalist concerned with medicines made from plants and animals, distinct from the sangoma who works through divination and the ancestors. CAPS Gr 4-6 Sosiale Wetenskappe, printed p. 45 (this very topic) says that indigenous healing TENDS to take a holistic approach ('is geneig om') and, in its first content cluster, that not all indigenous practices include spiritual healing and that many traditional healers use herbs and plants, not spirits. The holistic orientation is well attested as a TENDENCY of the tradition (Wikipedia 'African traditional medicine': imbalance between patient and social or spiritual world), but the sentence states it of all indigenous healing without a qualifier.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier, not the subject: say that indigenous healing usually or often looks at the whole person (is geneig om / kyk dikwels), so the sentence no longer says that all indigenous healing treats the spirit. As written it contradicts the sound fact that some healers, such as herbalists, work with plant medicines and do not treat the spirit, which a learner will meet elsewhere in this topic. Keep the rest of the description.

items.bewering: Daarby bevat inheemse genesing baie kennis van plante wat as medisyne gebruik word.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: Brendler & van Wyk 2008, J Ethnopharmacol (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18725280): several tuberous Pelargonium species are important traditional medicines with a rich ethnobotanical history; Wikipedia 'Traditional healers of Southern Africa': inyanga as herbalist working with plant and animal medicines.

items.bewering: Westerse medisyne word veral met siektes van die liggaam self verbind.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: Engel 1977, 'The need for a new medical model: a challenge for biomedicine', Science 196:129-136 (abstract via urmc.rochester.edu): the dominant biomedical model accounts for disease by measurable biological variables and leaves no room for social, psychological and behavioural dimensions. The 'veral' qualifier is appropriate.

items.bewering: Dit bou op wetenskap, tegnologie en kennis wat veral in Wes-Europa en Noord-Amerika gegroei het.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'western medicine': the standard medical treatment of Europe and North America, relying on scientific methods; Lock & Nguyen (summarised in journals.iea.ras.ru medical anthropology review) place the emergence of biomedicine in Europe and North America in the 19th century; NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, 'western medicine'.

items.bewering: Jy het hierdie kwartaal geleer van die groot ontdekkings wat daaruit gekom het.
items.blok: Twee maniere van genees in een land
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4-6 Sosiale Wetenskappe, printed p. 45: the same Grade 6 Term 4 topic teaches Jenner, Pasteur, Koch, Fleming and the first heart transplant, all discoveries of scientific Western medicine. A cross-reference within the term, consistent with the curriculum.

items.bewering: In die verlede het Westerse medisyne die skakel tussen die geestelike en die fisiese dikwels verwaarloos. 'n Dokter het na die siek deel van die liggaam gekyk en nie altyd na die hele mens nie.
items.blok: Wat Westerse medisyne vroeër oorgeslaan het
items.bron: Engel 1977, Science 196:129-136 (abstract via urmc.rochester.edu and psychotraumanet.org): the biomedical model left no room for the social, psychological and behavioural dimensions of illness. 'Dikwels' and 'nie altyd nie' are correctly hedged.

items.bewering: 'n Meer holistiese benadering is nou algemeen deel van die onderrig in die meeste Westerse mediese skole.
items.blok: Wat mediese skole nou ook leer
items.bron: LCME accreditation standards, Elements 7.1 and 7.2 (as quoted by UMass Chan and FIU medical schools): every accredited US and Canadian MD programme must teach behavioural and socioeconomic sciences and their impact on patients; Engel 1977 proposed the biopsychosocial model as a framework for teaching; University of Rochester describes it as a standard approach in many schools; Finnish case study (From biomedical teaching to biopsychosocial education) shows the same shift in Europe. CAPS printed p. 45 says the same. Caveat for the person reading: commentators (PMC7439629) say implementation is uneven and training still leans biomedical, but the lesson's claim is the modest comparative 'meer holisties ... deel van die onderrig', which accreditation requirements support.

items.bewering: 'n Student by so 'n skool word geleer om na die hele mens te vra. Hy vra ook na die mens se lewe, sy familie en wat hom pla. Hy vra nie net na die siek deel van die liggaam nie. Die siekte is dan net een deel van die hele storie.
items.blok: Wat mediese skole nou ook leer
items.bron: LCME Element 7.2 (UMass Chan 'Standard 7: Curricular Content'): students are prepared to recognise the health impact on patients of behavioural and socioeconomic factors; patient-centred, biopsychosocial history-taking described in PMC4711959 and PMC7439629.

items.bewering: Dit is wat die meeste mediese skole vandag vir nuwe dokters leer.
items.blok: Wat mediese skole nou ook leer
items.bron: Same basis as the item above on 'die meeste Westerse mediese skole' (LCME Elements 7.1/7.2; Engel 1977). In context it refers back to Western medical schools; it is accurate on that reading.

items.bewering: Baie mense in Suid-Afrika gaan na 'n kliniek of 'n dokter én na 'n tradisionele geneser.
items.bron: Pinkoane, Greeff & Koen 2012 (repository.nwu.ac.za/handle/10394/41445): 80-90% of black patients use both traditional healers and biomedical personnel; Frontiers in Public Health 2018 (10.3389/fpubh.2018.00073): traditional practitioner use continues despite wide ART availability.

items.bewering: Soms gebeur dit selfs met dieselfde siekte.
items.bron: Pinkoane, Greeff & Koen 2012: failure of one form of care to yield the expected result leads to use of the other; Puoane et al. 2017, BMC Complement Altern Med (PMC5577748): HIV-positive patients on ART who also use traditional medicine.

items.bewering: Party mense kry by die kliniek medisyne en gaan ook by 'n geneser hoor waarom hulle siek geword het.
items.bron: Burman & Aphane, African Journal of AIDS Research (Limpopo): patients move between a traditional and an allopathic explanation of what caused the disease; Wikipedia 'African traditional medicine' and 'Traditional healers of Southern Africa': healers seek the root cause of illness, often attributed to ancestors or the social and spiritual world. 'Party mense' is correctly hedged.

items.bewering: So raak die twee vorme van genesing mekaar by die pasiënt wat albei gebruik.
items.bron: Follows from the dual-use findings above (Pinkoane et al. 2012; Puoane et al. 2017).

items.bewering: Van die genesers en die werkers by 'n kliniek werk vandag saam. So 'n geneser stuur 'n siek mens soms na die kliniek toe. Hy doen dit wanneer hy sien dat die kliniek die regte plek vir daardie siekte is.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n geneser na die kliniek verwys
items.bron: Audet et al. 2017, BMC Complement Altern Med (Bushbuckridge): healers referred suspected HIV-infected patients to allopathic care; HSRC controlled study of an HIV/STI/TB intervention with traditional healers in KwaZulu-Natal (repository.hsrc.ac.za/handle/20.500.11910/6513); Health-e News, 4 October 2024: referral system between the health department and traditional healers, Mpumalanga healers referring HIV-positive patients to clinics.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit 'n verwysing wanneer 'n siek mens so na 'n ander plek gestuur word.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n geneser na die kliniek verwys
items.bron: Usage in the referral studies above (Audet et al. 2017; HSRC KZN study; Health-e 2024), where 'referral' means sending a patient on to the clinic for care.

items.bewering: Nie alle genesers werk so nie.
items.blok: Wanneer 'n geneser na die kliniek verwys
items.bron: PMC3731350 / PMC2816575: referral rates by healers were low; HSRC KZN controlled trial: referrals did not rise after training; Valley Trust study: collaboration limited and one-way.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het in 2007 'n wet gemaak wat tradisionele genesers erken.
items.bron: Traditional Health Practitioners Act, 2007 (Act No. 22 of 2007), source.acts.co.za; PMG bill history (pmg.org.za/bill/462): passed by the National Assembly on 20 September 2007 and by the NCOP on 22 November 2007. Note for the person reading: the President signed it on 6 or 7 January 2008 (PMG and the Act's own text differ by a day) and it was gazetted on 10 January 2008, so 'made in 2007' is right for Parliament and for the Act's name and number, but signing and publication fell in 2008.

items.bewering: Die wet het ook 'n raad vir hierdie genesers ingestel.
items.bron: Traditional Health Practitioners Act 22 of 2007, long title and section 4 (source.acts.co.za): 'To establish the Interim Traditional Health Practitioners Council of South Africa'.

items.bewering: Die werk van 'n geneser is daarmee 'n beroep wat die wet erken.
items.bron: Traditional Health Practitioners Act 22 of 2007, long title and section 2 (source.acts.co.za): provides for the registration, training and conduct of traditional health practitioners. The Act's provisions came into force in stages (2008, 2014, 2018), which does not affect the sentence.

items.bewering: Sommige plante wat genesers al lank gebruik, word vandag ook deur farmaseutiese maatskappye ondersoek. Party van hierdie plante word selfs as medisyne verkoop.
items.bron: Brendler & van Wyk 2008, J Ethnopharmacol (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18725280): Pelargonium sidoides, a southern African traditional medicine, was developed in Europe as Umckaloabo, with 18 clinical studies; marketed by Schwabe as extract EPs 7630 and sold as a medicine for acute respiratory infections (German pharmacy listings, docmorris.de).

items.bewering: Die geneser se kennis van plante en die navorser se werk kom hier by dieselfde plant uit.
items.bron: Brendler & van Wyk 2008: the commercial product grew out of the plant's ethnobotanical use; systematic review 'Pelargonium sidoides - from ethnopharmacology to evidence-based medicine' (dspace.nuph.edu.ua). The figurative 'kom ... uit' maps correctly: the same plant is the object of both traditional knowledge and laboratory research.

items.bewering: Die twee vorme van genesing bestaan vandag naas mekaar in Suid-Afrika. Nie een van die twee het die ander een vervang nie.
items.bron: Frontiers in Public Health 2018: traditional practitioner use continues regardless of wide ART availability; Pinkoane et al. 2012: 80-90% use both; Traditional Health Practitioners Act 22 of 2007 regulates traditional practice next to the biomedical system.

items.bewering: Hulle raak mekaar by die pasiënt en by die kliniek. Hulle raak mekaar ook by die wet en by die plante.
items.bron: Summary of the four points of contact verified above: dual use (Pinkoane et al. 2012), healer referral to clinics (Audet et al. 2017; HSRC KZN study), the 2007 Act (source.acts.co.za), and Pelargonium sidoides (Brendler & van Wyk 2008).

items.bewering: Holisties beteken om na die geheel te kyk en nie net na los dele nie, en by 'n mens is daardie geheel meer as sy liggaam alleen: ook sy gees, sy gevoelens en die mense om hom.
items.bron: Dictionary.com, 'holistic': relating to the whole rather than the parts; in medicine, care that looks at physical, psychological and social well-being rather than isolated diseases; Vocabulary.com, 'holistic': looking at the whole person rather than only physical symptoms. 'Gees' (mind/spirit) and 'die mense om hom' (social) map onto the psychological and social parts of the definition.

items.bewering: Wanneer 'n pasiënt na 'n ander plek of persoon toe gestuur word vir hulp.
items.bron: Usage of 'referral' in the South African healer-clinic studies above (Audet et al. 2017; HSRC KZN study; Health-e News 2024): sending a patient on to another provider or facility for care.

items.bewering: Wat met die maak van medisyne te doen het.
items.bron: Wiktionary, 'pharmaceutical': of or relating to pharmacy (the preparation and dispensing of medicines); ABP sector factsheet on pharmaceutical companies: they develop, produce and distribute medicines. The definition simplifies by leaving out dispensing, but it is accurate for 'farmaseutiese maatskappye', the only use in the lesson.

opsomming: Every claim checks out (including the 2007 Act, passed by Parliament in 2007 and signed in January 2008, and no comparison that teaches a false picture) except one: the opening block says without a qualifier that indigenous healing treats spirit and body together, while some healers, such as herbalists, treat only with plants (CAPS says so for this very topic), so that sentence must be narrowed to 'usually' or 'tends to'.
